audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel chapter 20, first-pass restored draft
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for David's danger assessment, Jonathan's changing belief, new-moon meal, covenant reciprocity, intergenerational protection, coded arrow signal, misogynistic insult, spear attack against Jonathan, child messenger, kissing, weeping, and queer-erasure/misuse.

verses.restored: David fled from Naioth in Ramah, came before Jonathan, and said, What have I done? What is my guilt and what is my sin before your father, that he seeks my life?

familiar.text: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said before Jonathan, What have I done? what is mine iniquity? and what is my sin before thy father, that he seeketh my life?

modern.text: Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah. He came to Jonathan and asked, “What have I done? What is my iniquity? How have I sinned against your father, that he wants to take my life?”

original.text: וַיִּבְרַ֣ח דָּוִ֔ד מנוות בָּרָמָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֞א וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן מֶ֤ה עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ מֶֽה עֲוֺנִ֤י וּמֶֽה חַטָּאתִי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ כִּ֥י מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת נַפְשִֽׁי

verses.restored: Jonathan said to him, Far be it! You shall not die. Look, my father does nothing great or small without uncovering my ear. Why would my father hide this matter from me? It is not so.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, God forbid; thou shalt not die: behold, my father will do nothing either great or small, but that he will shew it me: and why should my father hide this thing from me? it is not so.

modern.text: “Far from it!” Jonathan replied. “You will not die. Indeed, my father does nothing, great or small, without telling me. So why would he hide this matter from me? This cannot be true!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֣וֹ חָלִילָה֮ לֹ֣א תָמוּת֒ הִנֵּ֡ה לו עשה אָבִ֜י דָּבָ֣ר גָּד֗וֹל א֚וֹ דָּבָ֣ר קָטֹ֔ן וְלֹ֥א יִגְלֶ֖ה אֶת אָזְנִ֑י וּמַדּוּעַ֩ יַסְתִּ֨יר אָבִ֥י מִמֶּ֛נִּי אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אֵ֥ין זֹֽאת

verses.restored: David swore again and said, Your father surely knows I have found favor in your eyes, and he says, Let Jonathan not know this lest he be grieved. Yet as YHWH lives and as your life lives, there is but a step between me and death.

familiar.text: And David sware moreover, and said, Thy father certainly knoweth that I have found grace in thine eyes; and he saith, Let not Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved: but truly as the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, there is but a step between me and death.

modern.text: But David again vowed, “Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said, ‘Jonathan must not know of this, or he will be grieved.’ As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, there is but a step between me and death.”

original.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֨ע ע֜וֹד דָּוִ֗ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יָדֹ֨עַ יָדַ֜ע אָבִ֗יךָ כִּֽי מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וַיֹּ֛אמֶר אַל יֵֽדַע זֹ֥את יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן פֶּן יֵֽעָצֵ֑ב וְאוּלָ֗ם חַי יְהוָה֙ וְחֵ֣י נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ כִּ֣י כְפֶ֔שַׂע בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין הַמָּֽוֶת

verses.restored: Jonathan said to David, Whatever your life says, I will do for you.

familiar.text: Then said Jonathan unto David, Whatsoever thy soul desireth, I will even do it for thee.

modern.text: Then Jonathan said to David, “Whatever you desire, I will do for you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן אֶל דָּוִ֑ד מַה תֹּאמַ֥ר נַפְשְׁךָ֖ וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה לָּֽךְ

verses.restored: David said to Jonathan, Look, new moon is tomorrow, and I should sit with king to eat. Send me away, and I will hide in field until evening of third day.

familiar.text: And David said unto Jonathan, Behold, to morrow is the new moon, and I should not fail to sit with the king at meat: but let me go, that I may hide myself in the field unto the third day at even.

modern.text: So David told him, “Look, tomorrow is the New Moon, and I am supposed to dine with the king. Instead, let me go and hide in the field until the third evening from now.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן הִֽנֵּה חֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ מָחָ֔ר וְאָנֹכִ֛י יָשֹׁב אֵשֵׁ֥ב עִם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וְשִׁלַּחְתַּ֨נִי֙ וְנִסְתַּרְתִּ֣י בַשָּׂדֶ֔ה עַ֖ד הָעֶ֥רֶב הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁית

verses.restored: If your father misses me, say, David earnestly asked leave from me to run to Bethlehem his city, because yearly sacrifice is there for all clan.

familiar.text: If thy father at all miss me, then say, David earnestly asked leave of me that he might run to Bethlehem his city: for there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the family.

modern.text: If your father misses me at all, tell him, ‘David urgently requested my permission to hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because there is an annual sacrifice for his whole clan.’

original.text: אִם פָּקֹ֥ד יִפְקְדֵ֖נִי אָבִ֑יךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ נִשְׁאֹל֩ נִשְׁאַ֨ל מִמֶּ֤נִּי דָוִד֙ לָרוּץ֙ בֵּֽית לֶ֣חֶם עִיר֔וֹ כִּ֣י זֶ֧בַח הַיָּמִ֛ים שָׁ֖ם לְכָל הַמִּשְׁפָּחָֽה

verses.restored: If he says, Good, there is peace for your servant. But if his anger burns, know that harm is determined by him.

familiar.text: If he say thus, It is well; thy servant shall have peace: but if he be very wroth, then be sure that evil is determined by him.

modern.text: If he says, ‘Good,’ then your servant is safe, but if he is enraged, you will know he has evil intentions.

original.text: אִם כֹּ֥ה יֹאמַ֛ר ט֖וֹב שָׁל֣וֹם לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְאִם חָרֹ֤ה יֶֽחֱרֶה֙ ל֔וֹ דַּ֕ע כִּֽי כָלְתָ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ה מֵעִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Deal in covenant-kindness with your servant, for into covenant of YHWH you brought your servant with you. But if there is guilt in me, put me to death yourself; why bring me to your father?

familiar.text: Therefore thou shalt deal kindly with thy servant; for thou hast brought thy servant into a covenant of the LORD with thee: notwithstanding, if there be in me iniquity, slay me thyself; for why shouldest thou bring me to thy father?

modern.text: Therefore deal faithfully with your servant, for you have brought me into a covenant with you before the LORD. If there is iniquity in me, then kill me yourself; why should you bring me to your father?”

original.text: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ חֶ֨סֶד֙ עַל עַבְדֶּ֔ךָ כִּ֚י בִּבְרִ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה הֵבֵ֥אתָ אֶֽת עַבְדְּךָ֖ עִמָּ֑ךְ וְאִם יֶשׁ בִּ֤י עָוֺן֙ הֲמִיתֵ֣נִי אַ֔תָּה וְעַד אָבִ֖יךָ לָמָּה זֶּ֥ה תְבִיאֵֽנִי

verses.restored: Jonathan said, Far be it from you! If I certainly knew harm was determined by my father to come upon you, would I not tell you?

familiar.text: And Jonathan said, Far be it from thee: for if I knew certainly that evil were determined by my father to come upon thee, then would not I tell it thee?

modern.text: “Never!” Jonathan replied. “If I ever found out that my father had evil intentions against you, would I not tell you?” Jonathan and David Renew Their Covenant

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן חָלִ֣ילָה לָּ֑ךְ כִּ֣י אִם יָדֹ֣עַ אֵדַ֗ע כִּֽי כָלְתָ֨ה הָרָעָ֜ה מֵעִ֤ם אָבִי֙ לָב֣וֹא עָלֶ֔יךָ וְלֹ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ אַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ

verses.restored: David said to Jonathan, Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?

familiar.text: Then said David to Jonathan, Who shall tell me? or what if thy father answer thee roughly?

modern.text: Then David asked Jonathan, “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן מִ֖י יַגִּ֣יד לִ֑י א֛וֹ מַה יַּעַנְךָ֥ אָבִ֖יךָ קָשָֽׁה

verses.restored: Jonathan said to David, Come, let us go out to field. They both went out to field.

familiar.text: And Jonathan said unto David, Come, and let us go out into the field. And they went out both of them into the field.

modern.text: “Come,” he replied, “let us go out to the field.” So the two of them went out into the field,

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֽוֹנָתָן֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד לְכָ֖ה וְנֵצֵ֣א הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיֵּצְא֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם הַשָּׂדֶֽה

verses.restored: Jonathan said to David, By YHWH Divine of Israel: when I search out my father about this time tomorrow or third day, if there is good toward David, will I not send to you and uncover your ear?

familiar.text: And Jonathan said unto David, O LORD God of Israel, when I have sounded my father about to morrow any time, or the third day, and, behold, if there be good toward David, and I then send not unto thee, and shew it thee;

modern.text: and Jonathan said, “By the LORD, the God of Israel, I will sound out my father by this time tomorrow or the next day. If he is favorable toward you, will I not send for you and tell you?

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֜ן אֶל דָּוִ֗ד יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּֽי אֶחְקֹ֣ר אֶת אָבִ֗י כָּעֵ֤ת מָחָר֙ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֔ית וְהִנֵּה ט֖וֹב אֶל דָּוִ֑ד וְלֹֽא אָז֙ אֶשְׁלַ֣ח אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְגָלִ֖יתִי אֶת אָזְנֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Thus may YHWH do to Jonathan and thus add if harm seems good to my father against you and I do not uncover your ear and send you away, so you may go in peace. May YHWH be with you as he was with my father.

familiar.text: The LORD do so and much more to Jonathan: but if it please my father to do thee evil, then I will shew it thee, and send thee away, that thou mayest go in peace: and the LORD be with thee, as he hath been with my father.

modern.text: But if my father intends to bring evil on you, then may the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if I do not tell you and send you on your way in safety. May the LORD be with you, just as He has been with my father.

original.text: כֹּֽה יַעֲשֶׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה לִֽיהוֹנָתָ֜ן וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֗יף כִּֽי יֵיטִ֨ב אֶל אָבִ֤י אֶת הָֽרָעָה֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ וְגָלִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת אָזְנֶ֔ךָ וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֖יךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ֣ לְשָׁל֑וֹם וִיהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם אָבִֽי

verses.restored: And if I am still alive, will you not show me covenant-kindness of YHWH, so I do not die?

familiar.text: And thou shalt not only while yet I live shew me the kindness of the LORD, that I die not:

modern.text: And as long as I live, treat me with the LORD’s loving devotion, that I may not die,

original.text: וְלֹ֖א אִם עוֹדֶ֣נִּי חָ֑י וְלֹֽא תַעֲשֶׂ֧ה עִמָּדִ֛י חֶ֥סֶד יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א אָמֽוּת

verses.restored: Do not cut off your covenant-kindness from my house forever, not even when YHWH cuts off each enemy of David from face of ground.

familiar.text: But also thou shalt not cut off thy kindness from my house for ever: no, not when the LORD hath cut off the enemies of David every one from the face of the earth.

modern.text: and do not ever cut off your loving devotion from my household—not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.”

original.text: וְלֹֽא תַכְרִ֧ת אֶֽת חַסְדְּךָ֛ מֵעִ֥ם בֵּיתִ֖י עַד עוֹלָ֑ם וְלֹ֗א בְּהַכְרִ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת אֹיְבֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אִ֕ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה

verses.restored: Jonathan cut covenant with house of David, saying, May YHWH seek it from hand of David's enemies.

familiar.text: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, Let the LORD even require it at the hand of David’s enemies.

modern.text: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, “May the LORD hold David’s enemies accountable.”

original.text: וַיִּכְרֹ֥ת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן עִם בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד וּבִקֵּ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִיַּ֖ד אֹיְבֵ֥י דָוִֽד

verses.restored: Jonathan made David swear again by his love for him, because he loved him as he loved his own life.

familiar.text: And Jonathan caused David to swear again, because he loved him: for he loved him as he loved his own soul.

modern.text: And Jonathan had David reaffirm his vow out of love for him, for Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.

original.text: וַיּ֤וֹסֶף יְהֽוֹנָתָן֙ לְהַשְׁבִּ֣יעַ אֶת דָּוִ֔ד בְּאַהֲבָת֖וֹ אֹת֑וֹ כִּֽי אַהֲבַ֥ת נַפְשׁ֖וֹ אֲהֵבֽוֹ

verses.restored: Jonathan said to him, Tomorrow is new moon, and you will be missed because your seat will be empty.

familiar.text: Then Jonathan said to David, To morrow is the new moon: and thou shalt be missed, because thy seat will be empty.

modern.text: Then Jonathan said to David, “Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you will be missed if your seat is empty.

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמֶר ל֥וֹ יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן מָחָ֣ר חֹ֑דֶשׁ וְנִפְקַ֕דְתָּ כִּ֥י יִפָּקֵ֖ד מוֹשָׁבֶֽךָ

verses.restored: On third day go down quickly and come to place where you hid on day of deed, and remain beside stone Ezel.

familiar.text: And when thou hast stayed three days, then thou shalt go down quickly, and come to the place where thou didst hide thyself when the business was in hand, and shalt remain by the stone Ezel.

modern.text: When you have stayed three days, hurry down to the place you hid on the day this trouble began, and remain beside the stone Ezel.

original.text: וְשִׁלַּשְׁתָּ֙ תֵּרֵ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד וּבָאתָ֙ אֶל הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁר נִסְתַּ֥רְתָּ שָּׁ֖ם בְּי֣וֹם הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְיָ֣שַׁבְתָּ֔ אֵ֖צֶל הָאֶ֥בֶן הָאָֽזֶל

verses.restored: I will shoot three arrows to its side, as though shooting at a target.

familiar.text: And I will shoot three arrows on the side thereof, as though I shot at a mark.

modern.text: I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as if I were aiming at a target.

original.text: וַאֲנִ֕י שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הַחִצִּ֖ים צִדָּ֣ה אוֹרֶ֑ה לְשַֽׁלַּֽח לִ֖י לְמַטָּרָֽה

verses.restored: Look, I will send boy, saying, Go find arrows. If I expressly say to boy, Look, arrows are on this side of you; take them, then come, for there is peace for you and no matter, as YHWH lives.

familiar.text: And, behold, I will send a lad, saying, Go, find out the arrows. If I expressly say unto the lad, Behold, the arrows are on this side of thee, take them; then come thou: for there is peace to thee, and no hurt; as the LORD liveth.

modern.text: Then I will send a boy and say, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ Now, if I expressly say to him, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them,’ then come, because as surely as the LORD lives, it is safe for you and there is no danger.

original.text: וְהִנֵּה֙ אֶשְׁלַ֣ח אֶת הַנַּ֔עַר לֵ֖ךְ מְצָ֣א אֶת הַחִצִּ֑ים אִם אָמֹר֩ אֹמַ֨ר לַנַּ֜עַר הִנֵּ֥ה הַחִצִּ֣ים מִמְּךָ֣ וָהֵ֗נָּה קָחֶ֧נּוּ וָבֹ֛אָה כִּֽי שָׁל֥וֹם לְךָ֛ וְאֵ֥ין דָּבָ֖ר חַי יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: But if I say to youth, Look, arrows are beyond you, go, for YHWH has sent you away.

familiar.text: But if I say thus unto the young man, Behold, the arrows are beyond thee; go thy way: for the LORD hath sent thee away.

modern.text: But if I say to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then you must go, for the LORD has sent you away.

original.text: וְאִם כֹּ֤ה אֹמַר֙ לָעֶ֔לֶם הִנֵּ֥ה הַחִצִּ֖ים מִמְּךָ֣ וָהָ֑לְאָה לֵ֕ךְ כִּ֥י שִֽׁלַּחֲךָ֖ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: As for matter we spoke, I and you, look, YHWH is between me and you forever.

familiar.text: And as touching the matter which thou and I have spoken of, behold, the LORD be between thee and me for ever.

modern.text: And as for the matter you and I have discussed, the LORD is a witness between you and me forever.”

original.text: וְהַ֨דָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְנוּ אֲנִ֣י וָאָ֑תָּה הִנֵּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינְךָ֖ עַד עוֹלָֽם

verses.restored: David hid in field. New moon came, and king sat at food to eat.

familiar.text: So David hid himself in the field: and when the new moon was come, the king sat him down to eat meat.

modern.text: So David hid in the field, and when the New Moon had come, the king sat down to eat.

original.text: וַיִּסָּתֵ֥ר דָּוִ֖ד בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיְהִ֣י הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ על הַלֶּ֖חֶם לֶאֱכֽוֹל

verses.restored: King sat upon his seat as time after time, seat by wall. Jonathan arose, Abner sat beside Saul, and David's place was empty.

familiar.text: And the king sat upon his seat, as at other times, even upon a seat by the wall: and Jonathan arose, and Abner sat by Saul’s side, and David’s place was empty.

modern.text: He sat in his usual place by the wall, opposite Jonathan and beside Abner, but David’s place was empty.

original.text: וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ עַל מ֨וֹשָׁב֜וֹ כְּפַ֣עַם בְּפַ֗עַם אֶל מוֹשַׁב֙ הַקִּ֔יר וַיָּ֨קָם֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אַבְנֵ֖ר מִצַּ֣ד שָׁא֑וּל וַיִּפָּקֵ֖ד מְק֥וֹם דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: Saul spoke nothing that day, for he said, It is an accident; he is not clean, surely not clean.

familiar.text: Nevertheless Saul spake not any thing that day: for he thought, Something hath befallen him, he is not clean; surely he is not clean.

modern.text: Saul said nothing that day because he thought, “Something has happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean—surely he is unclean.”

original.text: וְלֹֽא דִבֶּ֥ר שָׁא֛וּל מְא֖וּמָה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא כִּ֤י אָמַר֙ מִקְרֶ֣ה ה֔וּא בִּלְתִּ֥י טָה֛וֹר ה֖וּא כִּֽי לֹ֥א טָהֽוֹר

verses.restored: On day after new moon, second day, David's place was empty. Saul said to Jonathan his son, Why has son of Jesse not come to food either yesterday or today?

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, which was the second day of the month, that David’s place was empty: and Saul said unto Jonathan his son, Wherefore cometh not the son of Jesse to meat, neither yesterday, nor to day?

modern.text: But on the day after the New Moon, the second day, David’s place was still empty, and Saul asked his son Jonathan, “Why hasn’t the son of Jesse come to the meal either yesterday or today?”

verses.restored: He said, Send me away, please, because our clan has sacrifice in city and my brother commanded me. Now if I have found favor in your eyes, let me slip away, please, and see my brothers. Therefore he has not come to table of king.

familiar.text: And he said, Let me go, I pray thee; for our family hath a sacrifice in the city; and my brother, he hath commanded me to be there: and now, if I have found favour in thine eyes, let me get away, I pray thee, and see my brethren. Therefore he cometh not unto the king’s table.

modern.text: saying, ‘Please let me go, because our clan is holding a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has told me to be there. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me go and see my brothers.’ That is why he did not come to the king’s table.” Saul Seeks to Kill Jonathan

familiar.text: Then Saul’s anger was kindled against Jonathan, and he said unto him, Thou son of the perverse rebellious woman, do not I know that thou hast chosen the son of Jesse to thine own confusion, and unto the confusion of thy mother’s nakedness?

modern.text: When the young man had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone, fell facedown, and bowed three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together—though David wept more.

familiar.text: And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as we have sworn both of us in the name of the LORD, saying, The LORD be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever. And he arose and departed: and Jonathan went into the city.

modern.text: And Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, for the two of us have sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘May the LORD be a witness between you and me, and between your descendants and mine forever.’” Then David got up and departed, and Jonathan went back into the city.

translation_notes: David directly names the threat to his life. Survivors may perceive danger before relatives or insiders are ready to believe them.
Jonathan initially trusts his father's usual disclosure, then tests the claim and changes his understanding. Loyalty and love require responsiveness to new evidence.
The covenant between David and Jonathan is reciprocal, intimate, political, and intergenerational. It may be explored without erasing queer readings or forcing a single modern identity label.
David's request that Jonathan kill him if guilty reflects extreme danger and ancient honor logic; it is not a model for suicide, assisted killing, or bypassing due process.
The new-moon plan uses concealment and coded signals for survival. People escaping violence are not morally required to disclose their location.
Saul's insult attacks Jonathan through misogynistic shaming of his mother and sexualized family honor. The unnamed mother is not responsible for the conflict.
Saul's claim that David threatens Jonathan's kingdom reveals dynastic fear. Political succession does not justify murder.
Saul hurls a spear at his own son. Jonathan's refusal to eat is grief and protest, not proof that fasting itself is spiritually superior.
The boy is used as an unwitting messenger; children should not be placed in dangerous adult conflicts or made carriers of secrets they cannot consent to.
The final kissing, weeping, oath, and separation express profound attachment. Their love is not shameful and must not be weaponized against LGBTQ people, friendship, masculinity, or faith.
'YHWH between us' makes the covenant accountable beyond immediate advantage; it does not make either man beyond later moral scrutiny.
safety_note: This chapter centers survival under domestic and political violence. Do not demand that endangered people reveal hiding places, reconcile with an armed abuser, or accept a broken family system for the sake of loyalty. Saul's misogynistic insult and spear attack are abuse. David and Jonathan's love must not be erased, mocked, sexualized against their will, or weaponized against queer people. Their death-language is not permission for suicide, honor killing, or private execution.
